extracted.intended_audience: legislators, patent practitioners, inventors, small businesses, and patent policy stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and policy standards for evaluating/structuring patent system reform (H.R. 1249/America Invents Act) focused on PTO funding, procedural changes (first-inventor-to-file, post-grant review, reexams), litigation rules, and protections for small inventors and universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allows the Director to adjust the fee schedule with appropriate congressional oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill allows the Director to adjust the fee schedule with appropriate congressional oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This authority is presented as enabling the PTO to become more efficient and productive, reducing wait time for patent approval and improving front-end patent quality. Adjusting fees is tied to funding PTO improvements and hiring examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevents Congress from spending agency funds on unrelated programs / ends fee diversion
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill prevents Congress from spending agency funds on unrelated programs by placing collected fees into a special fund to be used only by the PTO (fees still subject to appropriation but must be justified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as ending a 'hidden tax' on innovation caused by fee diversion (past diversions cited as $85–100M in a CR and nearly $800M over ten years). Ending diversion is argued to be essential to reducing backlog and pendency and to give certainty for PTO improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain 1-year grace period that protects universities and small inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: We retain both a 1-year grace period that protects universities and small inventors before they file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grace period protects disclosures by small entities and universities prior to filing. Some speakers proposed extending to 18 months to help small businesses obtain funding before filing; concern that changes to priority system must still protect small inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain CREATE Act protections for collaborative research
rubrics_metrics.description: Retains the CREATE Act, which ensures collaborative research does not constitute prior art that defeats patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves ability for collaborative research to proceed without creating prior-art issues that would harm patentability of resulting inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-inventor-to-file provision (shift from first-to-invent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Converts the U.S. patent system from a first-to-invent system to a first-inventor-to-file system, aligning U.S. law with international standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argued benefits: injects clarity and certainty, ends expensive interference proceedings, is faster and cheaper, allows priority via provisional filings, harmonizes with other countries. Also includes requirement for SBA/USPTO study to identify any negative impact on small inventors/universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust protection for prior user rights (including in the grace period)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be robust protection for prior user rights, including prior user rights in the grace period that exists under current law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concern raised that manager’s amendment lacks adequate prior-user protections (including trade secret-type prior uses). Prior user rights are necessary if moving to first-to-file to protect those who have been using the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow third parties to submit evidence of prior art during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislation allows third parties to submit evidence of prior art during the examination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a front-end quality improvement so examiners have a fuller record when making patentability decisions, thereby improving patent quality and reducing invalid patents being granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a new post-grant opposition system
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a new post-grant opposition system in which third parties can raise objections to a patent immediately after its issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-grant review is intended to help screen out bad patents while bolstering valid ones, improving overall patent quality and reducing downstream litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain inter partes re-exam process
rubrics_metrics.description: The legislation retains an inter partes re-exam process allowing innovators to challenge the validity of a patent when they are sued for patent infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an avenue for defendants to request the PTO take another look at a patent to better inform district courts about validity during litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow PTO to reexamine questionable business method patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill allows the Patent and Trademark Office to reexamine some of the most questionable business method patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to curb opportunistic use of business-method patents to extract payments from legitimate businesses; part of improving patent quality and preventing extortionate litigation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban tax strategy patents / deem tax strategies insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes a provision to ban tax strategy patents by deeming tax strategies insufficient to differentiate a claimed invention from the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justified as protecting taxpayers from monopolies on ways to comply with the Tax Code while balancing the ability of companies to develop tax-preparation and financial management software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit false marking private suits to those who've suffered competitive harm; retain government ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintains the government’s ability to bring false markings actions but limits private lawsuits to those who have actually suffered competitive harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to discourage opportunistic private litigants who have used false-marking suits to extract statutory damages without showing actual competitive harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict joinder rules in patent litigation to same facts and transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrict joinder of defendants to cases arising out of the same facts and transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed to end abusive practices of joining unrelated parties as codefendants simply to broaden litigation scope or pressure settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce backlog and pendency (quantitative targets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Targets: reduce pending claims to approximately 300,000 and average pendency to approximately 20 months (current cited ~700,000 pending and ~30 months average).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reducing backlog/pendency is tied to hiring additional examiners, improving examiner performance, and ensuring PTO has necessary funding and operational flexibility; presented as essential for small-business financing and job creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve patent quality on the front end to reduce litigation on the back end
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent quality will improve on the front end, which will reduce litigation on the back end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-end measures include third-party submissions, better-funded/examiner-resource PTO, improved examination processes, and post-grant review to prevent issuance of weak patents that fuel litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the small business ombudsman at the PTO permanent
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill makes the small business ombudsman at the PTO permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides small businesses with a constant champion at the PTO to look out for interests and assist in securing patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce fees for small businesses and independent inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: This bill protects small businesses and independent inventors by reducing fees for both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower costs are presented as a way to enable small entities to compete and to reduce barriers to obtaining patent protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require study of first-to-file effects on small inventors and universities
rubrics_metrics.description: A study regarding first-to-file will be conducted by the Small Business Administration and the United States Patent Office to identify any negative impact this change may have on small inventors and universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a safeguard to monitor unintended consequences of switching to first-inventor-to-file and to inform potential future adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance banning tax strategy patents with preserving access and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Language aims to ban tax strategy patents while preserving equal access to best methods of complying with the Tax Code and preserving the ability of companies to develop tax-preparation and financial management software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes striking a balance so the ban does not unduly hamper software innovation for legitimate tools and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide PTO tools and litigation reforms to increase certainty and attract investment
rubrics_metrics.description: By giving the necessary tools to the Patent Office to issue strong patents and by enacting litigation reforms, the bill will help inject certainty about the patents that emerge from this process—patent rights that are more certain to attract more investment capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument links improved PTO capacity and clearer post-issuance procedures to enhanced investor confidence, more investment, and economic growth across small and large firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend grace period to 18 months (proposed amendment for small businesses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal (offered as an amendment) to extend the grace period from 1 year to 18 months to help small businesses working to fund their patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed as a measure to protect small businesses that must seek funding and may need more time before filing; presented as not part of the manager’s amendment but as a suggested corrective.
